subject: Arborly vendor comparison & price-match request
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@arborly.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor economics — can Redwood match Nimbus?

Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — Elena and I ran the numbers and our CFO looped in procurement. We received a competing quote from NimbusAI that is materially cheaper for our expected 6–12 month pilot footprint.

High level: 1. Reserved commit (3mo) with moderate burst allowance; 2. Token pricing: $0.65 / 1k prompt, $0.90 / 1k completion; 3. Embedding bundle at $0.006 / embedding; 4. 12 TB egress cap for initial year. Nimbus is also offering a 20% implementation credit up front.

Can Redwood match or structure a package that is cost-competitive? Key constraints from our side: SOC2 in place, predictable monthly bill (we prefer committed buckets vs pure pay-as-you-go), and a short dedicated pilot window (2–3 weeks) before wider rollout.

I've attached the competitor quote we received (nimbus_quote-2027-07-18.pdf). If you can get a comparable economics + a short dedicated pilot we can move to contracting fast.

Thanks,
Samir Shah
Director of Product, Arborly Health
[sig] Samir Shah | samir.shah@arborly.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: nimbus_quote-2027-07-18.pdf (PDF, 47KB)

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the context and the quote. Short answer: yes, we can put together a package that is competitive, but it will be conditioned on mutually-agreed commit and a short pilot to validate throughput and latency SLOs.

Proposed next steps:
- Can you share a 30-day usage sample (qps, average request length, embedding volume)?
- We'll run an implementation-fit analysis and return a tailored offer (pricing + pilot details) by EOD today.
- If procurement needs SOC2 and an SLA template, I'll attach our standard materials and loop in Sales Ops.

I'll attach a preliminary price-match term sheet and a quick cost comparison for internal review — Lauren and Ben on this thread will handle the commercial and technical checks.

If you have 30 minutes this afternoon we can walk the numbers live.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Arborly — quick tech + econ notes (internal)

Internal — quick notes before we send the matched terms to Arborly: 

1) Ops/fit: Arborly's patterns (from demo) look like 60% short-chat gen, 30% embeddings, 10% long-form summaries. Their latency SLO is aggressive (p99 < 300ms for chat). We should propose a small Dedicated pool for the 2-week pilot to guarantee latency.

2) Cost delta: based on their projected monthly usage (est. 2.5B tokens/month + 250k embeddings), matching Nimbus as-is would reduce our ASP by ~17% vs our standard hosted SKU. We can bridge via:
   - 3-month commit at a 15% unit discount, plus
   - One-time onboarding credit equal to ~10% of committed spend, and
   - 2-week Dedicated pilot on us to prove latency.

3) Risk: egress is the big swing — if Arborly expects >10TB /mo, we need a hard egress surcharge cap or pass-through pricing. Recommend offering a 12 TB capped egress allowance for year 1 at flat $0 additional.

I've attached an internal spreadsheet with the economics scenarios (econ_compare_arborly.xlsx).

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: econ_compare_arborly.xlsx (Excel, 24KB) (internal)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@arborly.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@arborly.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor economics — can Redwood match Nimbus?

Samir / Elena —

Thanks for sharing the Nimbus quote. After a quick review with Solutions and Sales Ops, here's a commercially executable match we can offer to get you on a 3-month committed pilot: 

Offer (summary):
- Token pricing (pilot committed bucket): $0.55 / 1k prompt, $0.82 / 1k completion
- Embeddings: $0.0045 / embedding for the committed bucket
- 3-month minimum commit (auto-apply to month 1–3), with a 10% volume uplift credit if you exceed the commit by >25%
- Implementation/onboarding credit: 15% of committed spend applied as invoice credit over first 2 billing cycles
- 2-week Dedicated pilot: free — we will reserve a small dedicated GPU pool to guarantee p99 latency targets during pilot.
- Egress: 12 TB cap included for year one (any usage above billed at $0.08 / GB)

Conditions:
- Standard Redwood terms (we can add a limited SLA addendum); SOC2 report and current pen-test available on request.
- Pilot requires a signed mutual pilot agreement (term sheet attached) and a firm start date.

I've attached a redlined term sheet (redlined_term_sheet.pdf) with the numbers above and the pilot scope. Lauren from Sales Ops will send the formal deal in HubSpot. If these economics look good, can we lock a kickoff for next Monday?

Cheers,
Hannah

Attachment: redlined_term_sheet.pdf (PDF, 32KB)

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@arborly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@arborly.com>, Procurement <procurement@arborly.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor economics — can Redwood match Nimbus?

Hannah —

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn. Numbers look close. A couple of procurement asks before we can greenlight:
1) Procurement wants SOC2 + a signed data processing addendum.
2) They are asking for 2 months of cash-back credit (applied to first invoice) rather than the 15% invoice credit you proposed. That helps our burn model.
3) We need the egress cap locked in writing (they want a max liability cap).

If you can confirm SOC2 + DPA and move the onboarding credit to a 2-month cash equivalent, we can get the pilot signed this week. Attaching our procurement checklist for reference.

Samir

Attachment: arborly_procurement_checklist.pdf (PDF, 14KB)
